title: Lantern Rows
story: Each lantern in a row of n can be on or off, but two lanterns side by side may never both be on. How many different patterns are allowed? An empty row has one pattern: nothing. rows(left, on) counts the patterns for the lanterns still to place, where on says whether the last one placed is on.
hints: Place the lanterns one by one; what may come next depends only on how many are left and whether the last one is on.
An off lantern always fits: CALL rows(left MINUS 1, FALSE). An on lantern fits only after an off one: CALL rows(left MINUS 1, TRUE).
With no lanterns left there is exactly 1 pattern: stop at 0, not at 1, or an empty row never stops. The program asks rows(n, FALSE).
edgeCases: two lanterns on side by side
